data.title: Nasdaq futures surge as investors pile back into battered AI stocks
data.description:
Key points:
  • Futures up: Dow 1.33%, S&P 500 1.98%, Nasdaq 2.87%
  • Chipmakers, AI hyperscalers and neoclouds jump
  • Gold and silver miners rally tracking metals price recovery

By Shashwat Chauhan and Niket Nishant

US stock futures surged on Friday, led by a nearly 3% jump in Nasdaq 100 contracts, as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday to scoop up beaten-down AI-linked shares.

Wall Street's main indexes have swung sharply this week, with Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO and Anthropic's brief fall below its IPO price adding to volatility across the AI slide. Investors have alternated between bargain-hunting after a steep selloff and concerns over soaring costs, heavy borrowing.

"The recovery in stocks seems technical. The questions that caused the market panic are still unanswered," said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB. "If these gains can be sustained on Friday, it would suggest that enthusiasm for the AI trade is back."

Despite the turbulence, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are headed for their best week since August, while the blue-chip Dow is on track for its strongest week since April 2025.

The rebound has done little to erase November's losses. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq are on course for their worst November since 2008, pressured by concerns over tougher AI regulation following the Democrats' midterm election victory and expectations that monetary policy will remain restrictive.

Investors are also assessing the impact of the Trump administration's proposed new tariffs on imports from 14 trading partners, announced on Wednesday.

Traders are almost fully pricing in a Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December after data this week showed the US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter and inflation accelerated further in October.

All three major indexes entered a technical correction this month, with the Nasdaq at one point falling nearly 20% from its October peak.

At 04:23 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis (YMcv1) were up 669 points, or 1.33%, and S&P 500 E-minis were up 142.75 points, or 1.98%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 749 points, or 2.87%.

Nvidia, at the center of the AI boom, gained 4.7% in premarket trading, though the stock remained more than 37% below its October record high based on its last close.

Other chipmakers battered this month also rebounded, with AMD climbing 7% and Broadcom gaining 4.7%.

AI hyperscalers Alphabet , Amazon.com , Microsoft , Meta Platforms and Oracle rose between 2.3% and 5.3%.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave and Nebius advanced 7.9% and 9.5%, respectively. Other AI beneficiaries, including data-storage firm Sandisk, optical-products maker Lumentum and server maker Dell, also gained.

Gold and silver miners rallied as precious-metal prices recovered from a bruising few sessions. Newmont gained 5.6%, while the Global X Silver Miners ETF advanced 6.3%.

Vertex Pharmaceuticals fell 6.8% after the US Food and Drug Administration extended its review of the company's kidney-disease drug by up to three months.

Trading volumes could be light following Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday, with US equity markets open for only a half-day on Friday.

data.title: PSB Credit Growth Rises 18.8%, Net NPA Ratio Hits Historic Low Of 0.33%
data.description:
Gross advances reached Rs 127 lakh crore, while deposits increased 12.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 165.2 lakh crore in September

Public sector banks (PSBs) recorded an 18.8 per cent year-on-year growth in credit during the September quarter, taking their gross advances to Rs 127 lakh crore as of 30 September 2026. Their net non-performing asset (NPA) ratio also declined to a historic low of 0.33 per cent, reflecting an improvement in asset quality alongside rising lending activity.

According to data released by the Ministry of Finance on Thursday, total deposits of public sector banks increased by 12.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 165.2 lakh crore in September 2026. The Ministry attributed the growth in lending and improvement in asset quality to prudent credit practices, effective risk management and stronger recovery of bad loans.

Among major lending segments, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) recorded the highest credit growth at 20.4 per cent, followed by agriculture at 19.5 per cent. Corporate lending expanded by 19.1 per cent, while retail credit registered a growth of 17 per cent during the period.

Corporate credit growth has nearly doubled over the past 18 months, increasing from 10.02 per cent in March 2025 to 19.12 per cent in September 2026. MSME credit growth also accelerated from 13.12 per cent to 20.38 per cent during the same period, indicating stronger lending activity across business segments.

The Ministry said retail and agricultural credit had maintained strong growth for more than five years, while lending to MSMEs and corporates had also gained momentum and marginally outpaced other sectors. Among individual lenders, Bank of Maharashtra recorded the highest growth in advances at 22.5 per cent. Indian Overseas Bank followed with 17.9 per cent, while UCO Bank registered a growth of 17.5 per cent.

Asset Quality Improves Further

Despite the expansion in credit, public sector banks continued to report an improvement in asset quality. Fresh additions to bad loans, measured through slippages, stood at Rs 38,780 crore during the first half of FY2026-27, while the slippage ratio declined to 0.62 per cent from 2.35 per cent in FY2021-22.

The Ministry said all public sector banks had brought their slippage ratios below one per cent. This indicates a moderation in the pace at which standard loans are turning into non-performing assets, supporting the improvement in the overall health of bank balance sheets.

Early indicators of loan stress also showed improvement, with the ratio of Special Mention Account (SMA) category 1 and 2 loans above Rs 5 crore to total standard advances declining to 0.14 per cent as of September 30, 2026. The ratio stood at 0.24 per cent in the corresponding period last year. The outstanding amount under these stressed loan categories was Rs 18,800 crore, reflecting lower repayment stress in large loan accounts.

The Ministry attributed the improvement in public sector banks' financial performance to institutional reforms, stronger governance, prudent lending practices and efficient recovery mechanisms. These measures, it said, have helped banks expand credit while maintaining control over asset quality.

The Ministry added that stronger credit underwriting and risk management practices were creating a more resilient banking system, with the capacity to support the economy's long-term financing requirements.

data.title: US Tariff Threat Tests India’s $1 Tn Export Ambition, Seven Sectors Face Scrutiny
data.description:
With Washington proposing duties of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, exporters face questions over cost competitiveness and market diversification even as New Delhi pursues a bilateral trade agreement

The United States' proposal to impose tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods under its Section 301 investigation into alleged structural excess manufacturing capacity has put India's export competitiveness under scrutiny, with seven domestic manufacturing sectors potentially exposed to the proposed duties.

While Washington has indicated that the tariff could be reduced to 17 per cent if India concludes a trade agreement, the proposed differential has added another dimension to ongoing bilateral negotiations.

The investigation, initiated by the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) on 11 March, covers 16 economies, with proposed duties targeting 14 trading partners. The US has cited structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors as the basis for the investigation.

According to a report by the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), the Indian sectors flagged for potential excess capacity or export surpluses include solar modules, petrochemicals, steel, textiles, health-related goods, construction materials and automotive products. The report notes that India's solar module manufacturing capacity is nearly three times domestic demand.

The proposed tariff structure has also raised questions about the extent to which Indian exporters can absorb additional costs, pass them on to American buyers or redirect shipments to other markets without losing competitiveness.

Trade Deal Offers India Tariff Edge

The proposed 17 per cent tariff rate for India, compared with a possible 25 per cent without an agreement, is part of a dual-rate framework that offers lower duties to countries that reach trade agreements with Washington.

Pulkit Kapoor, SVP – Business & Economic Research, Axis Bank, said the proposed tariffs were intended to restore the tariff structure that existed before the US Supreme Court struck down reciprocal tariffs in February 2026.

"For India, the lower 17% tariff cap tied to a trade deal—versus a proposed default rate of up to 25% without one—improves marginally on the earlier 18% offer and keeps it relatively competitive among Asian peers," Kapoor said.

Under the proposed framework, India would have a 17 per cent rate if a trade agreement is finalised, against 18 per cent for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand, and 20 per cent for Vietnam and China. GTRI noted that the differential gives India a marginal tariff advantage over several competing Asian manufacturing destinations.

However, GTRI has questioned the rationale behind linking tariff relief to trade agreements rather than changes in manufacturing capacity.Its report argues that countries could secure lower tariff rates by offering trade concessions even if the industrial capacity cited in the investigation remains unchanged.

The report also warns that an adverse USTR determination could result in additional duties or import quotas. It further flags the possibility of Graham tariffs of up to 100 per cent, adding another layer of uncertainty to India's trade negotiations with Washington.

Manufacturing Sectors Under Scrutiny

The proposed investigation brings India's manufacturing expansion and export growth into focus, particularly in sectors where domestic production capacity has increased in recent years.

Solar modules are among the sectors specifically identified by GTRI, with the report pointing to manufacturing capacity nearly three times domestic demand. Petrochemicals, steel, textiles, health-related goods, construction materials and automotive products are the other sectors flagged by the US investigation.

The PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI), however, has contested the structural excess-capacity assessment.  "India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector," said Anil Gupta, President, PHDCCI, referring to the Department of Commerce's position in response to the USTR investigation.

He added that India's manufacturing expansion initiatives, including the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes and the Make in India programme, were designed to strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities, attract investments, promote technology adoption, generate employment and integrate Indian businesses into global value chains.

The chamber also identified electronic goods, drugs and pharmaceuticals, gems and jewellery, and textiles and apparel among India's leading exports to the US in FY2025-26. Together, these categories account for more than 50 per cent of India's exports to the American market.

PHDCCI said the price-stickiness of these products could limit the impact of tariffs in the short to medium term. However, the extent of the impact would also depend on how much of the additional duty exporters can absorb and whether US buyers are willing to bear higher import costs.

Export Diversification Gains Importance

The proposed tariffs come at a time when India is seeking to expand its export base and strengthen its presence across international markets. According to an Assocham report, India's total exports could reach USD 1,006 billion in FY2026-27, exceeding the USD 1 trillion target by USD 6 billion.

"Strengthening manufacturing capabilities, technology adoption, value addition and market access will be essential for translating India's export potential into sustained economic growth, employment generation and deeper integration into global value chains," Nirmal K. Minda, President, Assocham. The chamber's report projects merchandise exports at USD 561 billion in FY2026-27, representing year-on-year growth of 27 per cent.

The US is expected to remain India's largest merchandise export destination, with shipments projected at USD 102 billion, followed by the UAE at USD 34 billion, China at USD 24 billion and Singapore at USD 23 billion. The top 10 destinations are projected to contribute USD 263 billion, accounting for nearly half of India's merchandise exports.

However, the concentration of exports in a limited number of destinations could expose certain sectors to external trade disruptions.

The Assocham report identifies Singapore, Malaysia, Spain and South Africa as markets offering opportunities for diversification, with export growth of 108 per cent, 107 per cent, 88 per cent and 62 per cent, respectively.

It also highlights concentration risks in gems and jewellery and electrical machinery, where the top five destinations account for 78 per cent and 66 per cent of respective sectoral exports.

The chamber said technology upgradation, greater value addition, compliance with international standards and improved logistics would be important for sustaining export growth. Better access to export finance and effective utilisation of free trade agreements could also strengthen the competitiveness of Indian businesses, particularly MSMEs.

Trade Negotiations Remain Crucial

For India, the proposed tariff structure adds urgency to the ongoing negotiations for a bilateral trade agreement with the US. The government has maintained its commitment to working towards an early conclusion of the agreement, following the announcement made on 2 February 2026, and the joint statement issued on 7 February 2026.

PHDCCI said India would need to continue strengthening its manufacturing base while diversifying export destinations to reduce vulnerability to external disruptions.

The chamber also pointed to improvements in the ease of doing business, logistics efficiency and lower logistics costs as factors that could support supply-chain diversification.

"We are confident that government policy to boost exports through diversification by negotiating FTAs, robust domestic demand and boosting of in-house manufacturing capabilities will go a long way in maintaining India's resilience globally and stimulate business activity further," Gupta said.

GTRI, meanwhile, has argued that India should defend its manufacturing expansion sector by sector rather than allow export growth alone to be treated as evidence of excess capacity. Investments in manufacturing should be assessed against domestic requirements, overseas demand and future consumption.

As India works towards its USD 1 trillion export target and its longer-term ambition of USD 2 trillion in exports by FY2030-31, the proposed US tariffs present a challenge that extends beyond the immediate cost of duties.

The outcome of the trade negotiations, the final determination under the Section 301 investigation, and India's ability to diversify its export destinations will shape the competitiveness of its manufacturers in the American market and beyond.

Aditi Das

BW Reporters The author is a Trainee Correspondent at BW Businessworld. She is a postgraduate with a passion for research and storytelling. Curious by nature, she enjoys writing and exploring new ideas and perspectives.

data.title: Has organised crime penetrated South Africa's police and justice system?
data.description:
A South African judicial inquiry is examining allegations that criminal networks infiltrated the country's law enforcement system and built relationships with senior police officers, intelligence officials and political figures.

The Madlanga Commission, led by former Constitutional Court justice Mbuyiseli Madlanga, is due to submit its final report to President Cyril Ramaphosa on January 25, 2027, after an extension to consider further evidence and hear more witnesses.

Here is what prompted the commission, what it has uncovered during more than a year hearing evidence, and what is at stake.

HOW DID THE COMMISSION COME ABOUT?

The commission was triggered by allegations made publicly in July 2025 by KwaZulu-Natal police commissioner Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi, who said some politicians, members of law enforcement agencies, prosecutors and business people were operating in cahoots with criminal syndicates.

The commission is investigating whether criminal syndicates exert influence over a range of national and local authorities, including the police, prosecutors, intelligence services, judiciary and prison services.

It will look into claims of suppressed investigations, corruption, witness intimidation and the removal of officials, and whether senior officials helped criminal groups, ignored intelligence or benefited from their activities.

As its first witness, Mkhwanazi told the inquiry that the criminal justice system was "at real risk of total collapse", having faced threats and sabotage over an extended period.

This month, he was nominated as head of the country's specialised crime investigation unit, known as the Hawks, underscoring his prominence.

HAS SOUTH AFRICA BEEN HERE BEFORE?

South Africa has previously used judicial commissions to confront systemic corruption, most notably the Zondo Commission, which was established in 2018 to investigate "state capture".

Former President Jacob Zuma was jailed for contempt after defying an order to testify before that inquiry, and the sentence later barred him from standing for parliament in 2024.

The Zondo inquiry led to reforms, prosecutions and more than 16 billion rand ($912 million) in state-capture-related assets recovered by end-2025, according to the government.

While the Zondo Commission focused on corruption and political influence over state institutions, the Madlanga Commission is examining whether criminal networks have penetrated those institutions deeply enough to derail investigations, protect suspects and undermine law enforcement.

WHAT HAS BEEN REVEALED?

Mkhwanazi submitted a detailed statement and bundles of supporting documents setting out his allegations of criminal infiltration and interference with police investigations.

The commission has heard scores of witnesses over about 200 days of hearings, including senior national and municipal police officers, crime-intelligence personnel, investigators and people alleged to have links to criminal networks.

One figure who has featured repeatedly in testimony is businessman Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala. Messages recovered from his phones detailed links with senior police officers, including one who allegedly shared information about police investigations, and appeared to assist Matlala.

Another senior officer acknowledged that Matlala transferred 70,000 rand ($3,991) into his son's account, but said it was a loan that he repaid.

Others implicated in testimonies include officials accused of using their position to interfere in police operations or the outcome of tenders worth millions of rand.

Crime intelligence officer Feroz Khan and Ekurhuleni police official Julius Mkhwanazi, who have both been fired, faced allegations involving dealings with Matlala, while politically connected Brown Mogotsi featured in messages involving politicians, tenders and senior police.

Former Police Minister Senzo Mchunu, suspended after Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi's allegations sparked the inquiry, was accused of colluding with a criminal syndicate, and political interference over his decision to disband the Political Killings Task Team. Mchunu denied wrongdoing during his testimony, citing structural, budgetary and human-rights concerns.

Julius Mkhwanazi, who is not related to Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi, Matlala, and Mogotsi all denied any wrongdoing during their testimonies before the commission.

The allegations have not been established by the commission or tested in court.

WHAT IMPACT WILL IT HAVE?

The hearings have gripped South Africa, with explosive allegations of links between criminals, police and politicians drawing large audiences to live broadcasts on television and online.

The commission can recommend prosecutions and disciplinary action, as well as changes to legislation and institutions. Whether its revelations produce lasting change, however, will depend on what prosecutors, police leadership and the government do with its findings. ($1 = 17.5380 rand)

data.title: Graphite electrode demand set to rise by 1.50 lakh tonnes as global capacity shrinks: HEG Chairman
data.description:
Global demand for graphite electrodes is expected to increase by 1 lakh to 1.50 lakh tonnes over the next few years, supported by the expansion of electric arc furnace (EAF)-based steelmaking capacity and the closure of manufacturing facilities in developed markets, Ravi Jhunjhunwala, Chairman, HEG told businessline on the sidelines of its listing.

HEG Group has graphite as a separate business under HEG, which got listed on Friday at Rs 580 per share, while HEG Advanced Material with battery energy solutions, advanced materials, and green power businesses was listed in September.

Jhunjhunwala said that the demerger of HEG’s businesses was aimed at allowing two separately listed companies to focus on distinct growth opportunities.

While Bhilwara Group company HEG will concentrate on graphite electrodes, HEG Advanced Materials will pursue advanced materials, including graphite anodes and graphene, largely catering to the electric vehicle battery ecosystem.

The new entity has invested around ₹2,200 crore in its projects, with production expected to commence in about six months. The separation will allow investors to evaluate the two businesses independently, he added.

HEG Growth

On the HEG growth path, he said the global graphite electrode industry has seen the closure of around 1.50 lakh tonnes of manufacturing capacity over the last two to three years, taking total worldwide capacity down from about 6.50 lakh tonnes to nearly 5 lakh tonnes, Jhunjhunwala said.

The closures have largely been in the US, Europe and Japan, even as the world is adding around 100 million tonnes of new EAF-based steelmaking capacity.

“On one side, international capacities have closed down by about 1.50 lakh tonnes, while the world is adding 100 million tonnes of new electric arc furnaces,” he said.

Around 22-23 million tonnes of the proposed new EAF capacity has already been commissioned, while another 40-42 million tonnes is expected to come on stream over the next 18 months. The remaining capacity is likely to be added between 2028 and 2030.

Graphite electrodes are critical consumables in EAF steelmaking, with about 1.5 kg of electrodes required to produce one tonne of steel. The expansion of EAF capacity, therefore, is expected to significantly improve the demand-supply balance for manufacturers.

HEG, which currently has an installed graphite electrode capacity of 1 lakh tonnes, is operating at 93-95 per cent utilisation. The company is expanding capacity to 1.15 lakh tonnes, with the additional capacity expected to be ready by April-May 2028.

On raw material availability, Jhunjhunwala said needle coke, a petroleum-based critical input, was not a major concern as only three to four large refineries globally possess the technology to manufacture it. Power is another key input, with HEG requiring around 80-90 MW for its operations. The company’s Madhya Pradesh facility has had adequate power availability, he said.

data.title: Global brands shift hundreds of millions in orders from Bangladesh to India amid worker protests
data.description:
Global fashion retailers including Zara and H&M shifted nearly a tenth of ‌their monthly orders from Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs in the first half of November, as labour ​unrest disrupted production and rising costs eroded the country’s competitive edge, three factory owners said.

Between November 1 and ⁠18, brands diverted about $254 million worth of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said, in a shift that represents a major blow to a key pillar of Bangladesh’s economy and could extend beyond the current unrest.

Industry leaders have said rising wages, energy shortages and political uncertainty ‌have weakened the low-cost advantage that helped make Bangladesh the world’s second-largest apparel exporter after China, prompting global brands to diversify sourcing.

The protests have caused more than $400 million in production losses, according to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters ‌Association (BGMEA), in an industry that accounts for more than 80 per cent of Bangladesh’s export earnings and nearly 40 per cent of its manufacturing jobs.

India ‌has ⁠emerged as the biggest beneficiary of the order diversions, while buyers are also looking to Vietnam, Cambodia and ⁠Indonesia to reduce supply-chain risks and improve delivery reliability, industry leaders said.

Those pressures intensified on Wednesday when Bangladesh approved a 36 per cent increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, though the rise was the smallest in four decades.

The increase fell well short of workers’ demands to more than double wages, triggering fresh clashes with ​police even as Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the ‌Ministry of Labour and Employment, said the wage increase was “satisfactory” and that he hoped all garment workers would resume work from Saturday.

Industry leaders said the increase would nevertheless narrow Bangladesh’s labour-cost advantage over India, although union groups argue the wages remain low by global apparel industry standards.

The factory owners, speaking on condition of anonymity because of concerns about their relationships with international buyers, said the ‌unrest had prompted Zara, H&M, Marks & Spencer, Celio and other global brands to divert orders, with India receiving the ​bulk of the business.

Zara owner Inditex declined to comment on Reuters’ questions, while M&S, H&M and Celio did not respond to requests for comment.

M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury, a director of the BGMEA, said higher wages, utility and ⁠raw-material costs were adding to pressure on manufacturers.

“The wage increase has added to costs at a time when buyers are demanding lower prices and competition from rival sourcing countries is intensifying,” he said.

Mahmud Hasan Khan, the group’s president, declined to name the brands but said temporarily ‌shifting some orders elsewhere helps the industry retain global clients while minimising financial losses.

More business at risk

Factory owners said the bigger concern was that orders already diverted could be followed by the loss of future business as buyers reassessed where to source garments.

Persistent energy shortages, exacerbated by the Middle East crisis, have added to production disruptions and forced some factories to rely on more expensive alternative power sources.

Chowdhury said buyers were increasingly prioritising delivery times over price when choosing suppliers.

“Price becomes secondary when brands are under pressure to meet strict delivery deadlines,” he said.

India can offer buyers a delivery advantage of about a week, while Vietnam and Cambodia can cut lead ‌times by as much as 15 days, Chowdhury said.

Rival sourcing hubs can typically complete production and delivery within 60 to 90 days, compared with about 120 ​days in Bangladesh, he added.

The disruptions have also created production backlogs, with manufacturers around Dhaka losing an estimated 20 to 25 production days. Some are considering overtime and costly air freight to meet delivery commitments.

Khan Monirul Alam, ⁠managing director of Alps Apparels Group, which mainly supplies European brands, said the unrest was already hitting new business.

“Since November 1, most of my ⁠buyers have stopped placing orders because of the unrest,” Alam said. “They are telling us our orders have been shifted, postponed or cancelled and that they have already found alternative solutions.”

Political tensions surrounding former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s possible return to ‌Dhaka from India have added to concerns about further disruption.

Industry leaders said restoring stability and uninterrupted production would be critical to retaining international buyers. Chowdhury warned that orders shifted elsewhere during periods of instability might not return even after conditions improved.

“The challenge ​is restoring buyers’ confidence before temporary shifts become long-term sourcing decisions,” he said. “Brands have options. They will not wait for us if instability persists.”

data.title: Hong Kong's Yau Lee interim revenue falls 18%, profit rises

data.title: U.S. Treasury, European Bond Yields Rise as Investors Anticipate Fed, ECB Rate Hikes in December — Update
data.description:
By Emese Bartha

U.S. Treasury yields climbed on Friday as markets reopened for a shortened session following the Thanksgiving holiday, while European bond yields tracked them, driven also by higher oil prices.

The two-year Treasury yield rose 6 basis points to 4.693%, while the 10-year yield rose 7.4 basis points to 4.921%, according to Tradeweb. The 10-year German Bund yield moved 2.2 basis points higher to 3.279% and the 10-year U.K. gilt yield increased 4.4 basis points to 5.195%.

In the eurozone, a string of economic data has been released on Friday, including French and Spanish flash estimate inflation figures for November. Inflation in France decelerated faster than expected as fuel prices declined, to 3.2% on year from 3.7% in October and coming below the 3.6% rate expected by analysts in The Wall Street Journal's poll.

Inflation in Spain slowed to 4.1% in November from 4.9% in October, according to Spain's National Statistics Institute.

Despite the slowdown, the French and Spanish inflation prints remain uncomfortably high for the European Central Bank ahead of its December interest-rate decision. Money markets price in a 94% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike on Dec. 17, according to LSEG.

Investors in French bonds will watch S&P Global Ratings' scheduled review of France's A+ rating and stable outlook after market close.

Given the uncertain political backdrop, further budget slippage over the year and an eroding growth outlook, S&P may have enough reason to lower the outlook, ING senior rates strategists Benjamin Schroeder and Michiel Tukker said.

"At the same time, it would no longer really come as a surprise," they said in a note.

U.S. Treasurys face fewer immediate catalysts over the next few days after this week's economic data pointed to persistent inflation, resilient growth, and a solid labor market. Focus now shifts to the Federal Reserve's Dec. 9 interest-rate decision, where a 25-basis-point hike is fully priced, according to LSEG.

"Fed blackout period starts tomorrow so we are not going to get much information from them before the Federal Open Market Committee meeting," Jefferies economist Mohit Kumar said. "Our view remains that the Dec. 8-9 FOMC meeting should mark the peak in [the] Fed's hawkishness."

Jefferies doubts the Fed will match current market pricing, which anticipates 71 basis points of rate hikes by mid-2027, LSEG data show.

While the 10-year Treasury yield might have reached its cycle peak, it is premature to expect a sustained drop, SEB strategists Jussi Hiljanen and Filip Carlsson said.

"The bond rally since mid-November has been fueled by the equity selloff, perceived risks of overtightening and lower inflation expectations," they said. The strategists noted that stabilizing risk appetite could push yields back up, while continued caution would support bonds.

data.title: India's Economy Likely Grew 7.7% in July-September, WSJ Poll Shows — Market Talk
data.description: India's economy likely grew 7.7% in the July-September period from a year ago, slightly moderating from the 7.8% expansion seen in the previous quarter, according to the median estimate of eight economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. India's economy has held up relatively well despite continued headwinds, CareEdge says in a note. Economic growth was likely supported by encouraging activity in manufacturing, construction, and utilities, it says. Domestic demand remained strong, and real net exports likely contributed more to growth, although the drivers within each component are uneven, says ANZ's Dhiraj Nim. "While oil prices have receded recently, the geopolitical backdrop remains uncertain, and if oil prices stay elevated going into 2027, then downside risks to growth may start climbing again," BofA economists say. data.title: European Shares Extend Rally As AI Jitters Ease, Metal Prices Recover
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - European stocks surged on Friday, extending sharp gains from the previous session, led by mining and technology stocks.

Copper and gold prices recovered, helping spur a rally in the mining sector. AI-driven market jitters eased after authorities in South Korea and China announced support measures.

The pan-European STOXX 600 surged nearly 1 percent to 643.06 after climbing 1.8 percent in the previous session.

The German DAX rose 0.9 percent, France's CAC 40 gained 0.3 percent and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 added 0.6 percent.

Mining stocks such as Anglo American, Antofagasta and Glencore were up 4-5 percent after copper surged the most since January.

Precious metal miner Fresnillo soared more than 6 percent as gold prices jumped more than 3 percent on a softer U.S. dollar and improving technology sentiment.

Energy stocks such as BP, Shell and Total Energies all rose around 1 percent as both Brent and WTI remained on track for their first weekly gain this month due to rising attacks on energy infrastructure in the Middle East and vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

In the technology sector, Infineon Technologies, Aixtron and ASML Holding climbed 4-5 percent.

Schneider Electric advanced 1.6 percent as Shelly Group's board reaffirmed its support for the French energy technology company's amended offer.

German automotive supplier Stabilus rallied 2.6 percent after extending its contract with CEO Michael Buechsner for another three years.

data.title: EM stocks head for best week since June as bargain hunters return
data.description:
Key points:
  • MSCI EM stock index rises 1.9%
  • Turkish central bank suspends one-week repo auctions
  • OPEC+ meet expected on Sunday

By Niket Nishant

Emerging market stocks were on track for their biggest weekly gain since June on Friday as dip-buying and promises of policy support boosted bourses in Asia despite tariff threats from Washington.

Equities in emerging Europe, which are less exposed to the AI boom, have also recovered this week due to a risk-on mood in global markets.

The gains could help regional stocks recover some poise at the end of a tumultuous month that saw AI fears come to the fore as chip heavyweight Nvidia's leadership turmoil and Anthropic's rocky first week as a public company kept investors on edge.

The fallout of Turkey's investment fund scandal has also added to the unease, with the country's main stock benchmark on course for its second consecutive week of losses.

The index was up about 1% on the day, while the lira weakened 0.2%.

Turkey's central bank suspended its one-week repo auctions temporarily in a move expected to push overnight interest rates towards the 39% overnight lending rate, tightening liquidity after heavy forex sales and a sharp fall in reserves.

MSCI's index of emerging market equities CBOE:EFS rose 1.9% on Friday, while the currency gauge (.MIEM00000CUS) gained 0.3%. Both were headed for weekly gains, with the stock index on course for its biggest jump since June.

South Korea's KOSPI rose over 4% as hopes of market-stabilising measures supported dip-buying around 10-month lows.

Chinese stocks, and the yuan , also rallied after Premier Li Qiang chaired a State Council meeting that called for a bigger role by "national team" investors to stabilise a falling stock market.

ALL EYES ON OIL

Investors also kept an eye on oil prices, which were on course to snap a three-week streak of declines.

Brent crude futures have risen over 5% so far this week as attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil supplies out of the Middle East.

OPEC+, which comprises members of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies including Russia, is meeting on Sunday to decide the production strategy for next year.

"The group is expected to consider keeping current production quotas unchanged through January, although some members have been pushing for higher quotas," ING strategists wrote.

EM EUROPE ASSETS GAIN

In Poland, stocks rose 1.5% while the Polish zloty strengthened 0.2% versus the euro.

"There is little evidence that the energy shock is feeding through into broader price pressures in Poland," said Liam Peach, senior emerging markets economist at Capital Economics, while noting that the pressure to hike rates has eased.

Separately, the deputy head of Poland's central bank has warned that any attempt to bring Governor Adam Glapinski before the country's State Tribunal would be illegal and would undermine the stability of the central bank.

In Hungary, stocks rose 2.5%. The forint also gained 0.22%.

Data from economic think tank GKI on Thursday showed Hungarian business and consumer confidence both deteriorated in November, with consumer confidence falling to a seven-month low.

Meanwhile, Fitch Ratings affirmed Zambia's sovereign credit rating at 'B-' with a stable outlook, citing a debt burden that was elevated, but declining.

data.title: Inflation Slides in France, Spain on Declining Fuel Prices — 3rd Update
data.description:
By Ed Frankl and Paul Hannon

The annual rate of inflation in France and Spain fell more sharply than expected in November as fuel prices declined, while the eurozone economy grew less rapidly than previously estimated in the three months through September.

Investors expect the European Central Bank to raise its key interest rate next month for a third time since the start of the war between the U.S. and Iran. But the central bank has said it will be "data-dependent" in its policy decisions, and the latest readings from the eurozone economy point to weaker inflationary pressures.

Consumer prices in the eurozone's second-largest economy were 3.2% higher than in the same month of 2025, a lower annual rate of inflation than the 3.7% recorded in October, France's statistics office said Friday. Economists polled last week by The Wall Street Journal expected a 3.6% rate of inflation.

In Spain, figures also published Friday showed the annual rate of inflation also dropped sharply in November, to 4.1% from 4.9% in October.

Oil prices have fallen since the outcome of U.S. midterm elections fueled hopes of a lasting resolution to the conflict, although they remain above prewar levels. As a result, prices of gasoline and other fuels have declined.

However, European natural gas prices remain near multiyear highs, which will keep household energy prices elevated throughout the colder winter months.

The ECB has raised its key rate twice so far this year, judging that the surge in energy prices was too great to ignore. Investors are primed for another hike before the end of the year.

The EU said last week that it expects French inflation to peak at 4.3% in the first quarter of 2027 due to further increases in energy prices and how they pass through into food and services.

Yet incoming data shows few signs of those energy costs spilling over into other parts of the economy. Services inflation in France fell in November due to a sharp decrease in prices for accommodation and transport services.

Revised figures for economic growth in the three months through September indicate that the eurozone economy has been less resilient in the face of higher energy prices than previously estimated.

The French statistics agency on Friday said the country's gross domestic product sank 0.2% in the third quarter, having previously estimated the drop at 0.1%. Earlier this week, Germany's statistics agency cut its estimate for third-quarter growth.

"A weakening labor market and growing fears of unemployment will keep households cautious. At the same time, weak demand and a lack of visibility will continue to weigh on business investment. The outlook for 2027 remains very gloomy," Charlotte de Montpellier, an economist at ING, wrote in a note to clients.

French consumer spending was flat in October, data also published Friday showed. While surveys of purchasing managers for November showed steady economic growth in Germany, there was a deepening downturn in activity in France.

Amid those signs of weakening inflationary pressures, the ECB's own survey of 19,000 consumers between Oct. 1 and Nov. 2 yielded some concerning news for policymakers. It found that households expected prices to rise by 3.5% over the coming 12 months, up from 3.1% in September.

However, expectations may fall back in response to November's inflation figures, although the next survey won't be released until early next year and the ECB announces its policy decision on Dec. 17.

data.title: Sigma Solve H1 profit jumps 64% to ₹19.4 cr as other income boosts earnings
data.description:
Sigma Solve Ltd, an information technology and IT-enabled services company, reported a 63.89 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit for the first half of FY27, even as revenue from operations remained virtually unchanged, with a sharp increase in other income contributing to higher overall income.

The Ahmedabad-based company, listed on the NSE and BSE, reported consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of ₹19.40 crore for the six months ended September 30, 2026, compared with ₹11.84 crore in the corresponding period last year, according to a company statement.

Consolidated total income rose 12.71 per cent to ₹56.30 crore from ₹49.95 crore a year earlier. However, revenue from operations inched up just 0.44 per cent to ₹46.45 crore from ₹46.24 crore, indicating that the improvement in overall income was largely supported by non-operating income rather than growth in the company's core business.

Other income more than doubled to ₹9.86 crore from ₹3.71 crore in the year-ago period, accounting for 17.5 per cent of consolidated total income, compared with about 7.4 per cent a year earlier.

The company's consolidated earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 29.05 per cent to ₹16.27 crore from ₹12.60 crore. The EBITDA margin, calculated as a percentage of revenue from operations, expanded to 35.02 per cent from 27.26 per cent, an improvement of 7.76 percentage points.

Profit before tax rose 64.26 per cent to ₹25.67 crore from ₹15.63 crore in the corresponding period of FY26.

The PAT margin increased to 41.76 per cent from 25.60 per cent.

While the consolidated numbers point to a substantial improvement in profitability, Sigma Solve's standalone financial performance was comparatively subdued.

Standalone revenue from operations declined to ₹16.29 crore in H1 FY27 from ₹19.21 crore a year earlier. Total income fell to ₹16.99 crore from ₹20.07 crore.

Standalone EBITDA decreased to ₹3.95 crore from ₹4.14 crore, while profit after tax declined to ₹3.01 crore from ₹3.18 crore.

Sigma Solve said it would continue to strengthen its technology capabilities, expand its service portfolio and improve execution to address changing enterprise technology requirements.

The company operates across enterprise software development, cloud solutions, data engineering, business intelligence, analytics, artificial intelligence-driven solutions, digital transformation and automation.

These areas are increasingly central to corporate technology spending as businesses look to modernise legacy systems, automate workflows, improve operational efficiency and deploy data-driven applications.

Commenting on the results, Prakash R. Parikh, Chairman and Managing Director of Sigma Solve, said: "We remain focused on strengthening our technology capabilities, expanding our service portfolio and capitalising on emerging opportunities across Artificial Intelligence, digital transformation and enterprise technology solutions. Our focus continues to be on deepening client relationships, enhancing execution capabilities and delivering technology solutions that address the evolving needs of businesses. We remain committed to building a scalable business platform and creating sustainable long-term value for our stakeholders."

Separately, Sigma Solve said it had recommended a final dividend of ₹0.50 per equity share of Re 1 face value for FY26, representing a 50 per cent dividend on face value. The payout was subsequently approved by shareholders at the company's annual general meeting in September 2026.

The company said it had declared dividends in each of the four consecutive years since its listing in June 2023, highlighting its stated focus on shareholder returns alongside business expansion.

Incorporated in Ahmedabad on April 29, 2010, Sigma Solve provides enterprise technology solutions through its Indian operations and wholly owned US subsidiary, Sigma Solve Inc. Its offerings span software development, cloud computing, data engineering, analytics, AI-led applications and business process automation.

data.title: Stock Futures Jump as AI Trade Set for Rebound
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

U.S. stock futures are poised to open in the green for a shortened trading session Friday, as the artificial-intelligence trade rebounds at the end of a volatile week.

Nasdaq futures trade 2.7% higher, while contracts tied to the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.8% and 1.15% respectively. Stocks across the AI ecosystem rallied premarket, with Nvidia gaining around 4.5%.

Signs of a rebound follow choppy trade earlier in the week. However, the AI trade isn't out of the woods yet, XTB research director Kathleen Brooks said.

"While technical indicators suggest that a recovery could be on the cards, the fundamental problems surrounding the AI trade remain," Brooks said. "The questions that caused the market panic are still unanswered, for example, concerns about the profitability of the AI trade and financing costs."

Gains in the U.S. premarket followed a bullish session in Asia. South Korea's memory chip-dominated Kospi jumped 4.3%, while stock indexes in Shanghai and Hong Kong rose after Chinese authorities reiterated their support for capital markets. European equity indexes rallied at the open, with AI-related stocks leading the charge. The continent's Stoxx 600 index rose 0.95% in early trade.

Improved sentiment in equity markets bled into metals, too. Silver contracts jumped more than 10% to $44.11 a troy ounce, while gold futures added close to 4% to trade around $3,680 an ounce.

Oil prices continued to rise, with benchmark Brent crude contracts gaining 1% to trade around $97.50 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate contracts jumped 2.6% to trade around $85.90 a barrel.

Treasurys weakened amid investors' shift back to risk and hardened expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike next month. Ten-year yields rose more than seven basis points to trade above 4.900%, while two-year yields rose toward 4.700%. The Fed enters a blackout period on Saturday ahead of its December meeting, with expectations for a 25 basis point rise priced in at 99%, according to LSEG.

The dollar edged higher against a basket of global currencies but remained below highs hit earlier this week. Bitcoin was helped by broader ebullient market sentiment, rising 1.5% to trade around $61,670.

Spanish voters head to the polls on Sunday as Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez looks to stay in power. Next week, Nvidia's reinstated Chief Executive Jensen Huang will appear in front of Congress on Tuesday and Wednesday.

data.title: Global equity funds log biggest weekly outflow in 14 months
data.description:
Global equity funds recorded their largest weekly outflow in 14 months in the week to November 25 as growing concerns over returns on investments in the AI build-out and hawkish comments from US Federal Reserve officials dampened appetite for risk assets.

Investors liquidated a net $22.73 billion from global equity funds during the week, marking their largest weekly net sales since September 17, 2025, LSEG Lipper data showed.

Fund investors turned cautious last week as a technology selloff, driven by concerns over returns on AI infrastructure investments, pushed global stock indexes to seven-month lows.

The MSCI All Country World Index EURONEXT:IACWI fell to 1,019.01 last week, its lowest level since April 8. The index has, however, recovered about 3.5% so far this week.

"We estimate that overall revenues for AI models and applications will have to grow at least 750% over the next four years for the industry to earn an adequate return to justify the cumulative spending," said Mark Haefele, chief investment officer at UBS Global Wealth Management, in a note on Thursday.

"We maintain a Neutral view on global and US equities, reflecting a balanced risk-reward outlook."

US equity funds recorded net weekly outflows of $30.57 billion, the largest since September 9. Investors also withdrew a net $2.75 billion from Asian funds but added $7.29 billion to European funds.

Among sector funds, technology, healthcare and industrial funds came under pressure, with investors pulling a net $7.57 billion, $3.04 billion and $2.56 billion, respectively.

Global bond funds recorded a third consecutive weekly outflow, totalling a net $3.51 billion.

Investors sold a net $5.85 billion from dollar-denominated medium-term bond funds, $2.73 billion from euro-denominated bond funds and $1.54 billion from high-yield bond funds. However, they bought a net $7.14 billion of government bond funds and $1.17 billion of short-term bond funds.

Money market funds posted a third straight weekly outflow, totalling a net $49.42 billion.

Among commodity funds, gold and other precious metals funds recorded net outflows of $2.14 billion, their largest since March 25. Energy funds also saw outflows of $463 million.

In emerging markets, equity funds attracted a net $971 million for an eighth consecutive week. Bond funds, however, posted a fifth straight weekly outflow of $1.42 billion, based on data covering 29,180 funds.
